lecture_lines: Shrinking bars bridge to continuous variables.
A smooth curve represents the limit.

sections.title: Defining the Probability Density Function (PDF)
lecture_lines: PDFs measure probability density, not probability.
Think of density as scattered gold dust.
Probability is the area under the curve.
animations: Title: 'Defining the PDF' in #FFFFFF.
Draw Y-axis labeled 'Density' and X-axis labeled 'Value'.
Plot a smooth continuous curve in #00CED1.
Highlight point 'x' on axis, label 'f(x)'.
Connect f(x) to the curve with a dashed line.

sections.title: Core Properties & Visual Constraints
lecture_lines: Total area must equal exactly one.
animations: Title: 'PDF Core Properties' in #FFFFFF.
Show entire curve, label 'Non-negative: f(x) >= 0'.
Highlight whole area, label 'Total area = 1'.
Flash area under f(x) to emphasize integral definition.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: Area under the curve defines probability.
Single point probability is always zero.
Normalization ensures total area is one.
